title: Torsion sections are detected at the generic point
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$, let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], let $U\subseteq X$ be a nonempty open, and let $s\in\mathcal F(U)$. For $x\in U$, call the germ $s_x$ torsion if some nonzero element of the domain $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ annihilates it. Then the following are equivalent: (1) $s_x$ is torsion for some $x\in U$; (2) $s_x$ is torsion for every $x\in U$; (3) the germ $s_\eta$ is zero in $\mathcal F_\eta$; (4) the image of $s$ in $(j_*\mathcal F_\eta)(U)$ is zero, where $j:\operatorname{Spec}k(X)\to X$ is the generic-point morphism and $k(X)=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$.

proof.text: Fix $x\in U$. By quasi-coherence [pqf-def-coherent], choose an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $x$ with $\mathcal F|_W=\widetilde M$ for an $A$-module $M$. Since $W\cap U$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ in $W$, choose $f\in A$ with $x\in D(f)\subseteq W\cap U$ (principal opens form a basis). The open $D(f)$ is nonempty, so it contains $\eta$ because $X$ is integral. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], the map $\tau_{D(f)}:M\to\widetilde M(D(f))$ is localization at the powers of $f$; hence for $s|_{D(f)}$ there are $m\in M$ and $k\ge 0$ with $f^k s|_{D(f)}=\tau_{D(f)}(m)$. As $f$ is invertible on $D(f)$, its germs $f_x$ and $f_\eta$ are units, so $s_x$ (resp. $s_\eta$) is torsion (resp. zero) exactly when the corresponding germ of the section $\tau_W(m)$ is torsion (resp. zero). Now apply [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-stalk-localization] on $\operatorname{Spec}A$ to $\tau_W(m)$ at $\mathfrak p_x$ and at $(0)$; [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] identifies the latter localization's fraction field with $k(X)$.

proof.text: If $s_\eta=0$, Step 1 and the localization criterion for $m/1=0$ in $M_{(0)}$ give $a\in A\setminus\{0\}$ with $am=0$. The germ $a_x$ kills the germ of $\tau_W(m)$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], and hence kills $s_x$ because $s_x=f_x^{-k}(\tau_W(m))_x$ with $f_x$ a unit. Its germ $a_x$ is nonzero in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ because the map $A\to\mathcal O_{X,x}\to k(X)$ is injective [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]. As $x$ was arbitrary, (3) implies (2).

proof.text: If $s_x$ is torsion for some $x\in U$, take $0\neq b\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $b s_x=0$. The germ map $\rho_x:\mathcal O_{X,x}\hookrightarrow k(X)$ of [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field] sends $b$ to a nonzero element of the field $k(X)$, hence to a unit. Applying the compatible map $\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal F_\eta$ to $b s_x=0$ gives $\rho_x(b)s_\eta=0$, hence $s_\eta=0$. Thus (1) implies (3).

source.place: Tag 0AXR, lemma-torsion-sections, implication (1) to (3); proof omitted, germ calculation supplied here

proof.text: The open $U$ is nonempty, so (2) implies (1). Since $\eta\in U$ and $s_\eta=0$ is killed by $1\in\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$, (3) also directly implies (1). For the generic-point morphism $j:\operatorname{Spec}k(X)\to X$, its inverse image of any nonempty open $U$ is its one-point source, so $(j_*\mathcal F_\eta)(U)=\mathcal F_\eta$ and the image of $s$ is exactly $s_\eta$. Thus (3) and (4) are equivalent, finishing all four equivalences.
